questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, over how many cooldowns, and how many showed the e/4 gate period? The Methods describe "The device" (p. 9), while the author contributions say "M.D.L. fabricated the devices" (p. 9).
Why were the other devices or cooldowns set aside?

Which ranges of side-gate voltage, magnetic field and antidot-gate voltage did you measure at ν = −5/2, −1/2 and 3/2 beyond the ones shown, and in how many of those settings did the e/4 period appear?
What does the second-best e/4 dataset at each even-denominator filling look like, for example a Vadg-B map at a second side-gate setting within the minimal-excitation regime?

Most field scans have "typically NB ≈ 101 points per scan" at 1 mT steps (p. 10), about 2.5 periods of ∆B1 = 40.3 mT, and at ν = −1/2 in the doubled regime "there is no full magnetic field period present in the data" (Fig. S9, p. 21). Could you take wider field scans, and report the sign of the stripe slope in each map next to ν = −1, which Halperin et al. use to tell the two regimes apart?

Did you repeat fixed-field sweeps at the even-denominator states, as you did at ν = 2/3 (Fig. S13), and check gate leakage at base temperature? A nearby trap could add jumps that the 2D-FFT reads as a period.

The suppression temperature of the e/4 oscillations reads "approximately 60 mK" (p. 8), "between 50 mK and 70 mK" (p. 28) and "30 mK to 50 mK" (p. 30). Which applies? And since the doubled oscillations at ν = 2/3 "also remain finite up to 120 mK" (p. 28), how does that bear on reading the 120 mK persistence at ν = −1/2 as a different mechanism (p. 8)?

At ν = −1/3, Fig. S7 shows side-gate voltages of −2 V and 0 V, while p. 8 says "Even at the largest side-gate voltage accessible in our device, no period doubling is observed". What was the largest side-gate voltage reached at ν = −1/3?
